bug_semantics: GitPython's config writer interpolates option names verbatim into git-config lines (`write_section` emits `\t%s = %s\n`). Through 3.1.57, `_assure_config_name_safe(option, "option")` rejected only CR/LF/NUL, so `=`, `#`, `;`, brackets, and whitespace in an option name were accepted. A caller-controlled name such as `sshCommand = touch /tmp/RCE #` is written as `\tsshCommand = touch /tmp/RCE # = <value>`, which git parses as `core.sshCommand=touch /tmp/RCE` (the `#` comments out the intended value). That forges `core.sshCommand` / `core.hooksPath` / `alias.*` and yields RCE on a later git operation. Distinct field and character class from section-header bracket injection and from newline injection.
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism is unvalidated option-name serialization, first written when GitConfigParser._write/write_section was implemented in 3fd37230e76a014cf5c45d55daf0be2caa6948b7 (2009-10-19, lib/git/config.py:265). Immediate parent 9513aa01fab73f53e4fe18644c7d5b530a66c6a1 had only a stub write() and no format sink. Later CR/LF/NUL name checks (54538428f79b0c91ba52cda5229856a6edf7ac06) and section-only delimiter checks (1ed1b924f4e2d2ee7bab296df77b978af21853f1, gated on label=="section" and explicitly preserving option-name behavior) did not introduce this character class and did not close it. Encoding, black, and multi-value edits are refactors of the same key interpolation.
